behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Creates user-level persistence by writing a REG_SZ value under the current user's Run key. The value name is derived from the system MachineGuid and the value data points to a controlled marker executable placed in C:\Users\Public. On user logon or reboot, Windows automatically launches the marker executable, which writes a benign confirmation artifact for dynamic analysis.

persistence_installer.role: retrieves the MachineGuid, normalizes it, opens or creates the HKCU Run key, and writes a persistence value pointing to the marker executable

marker_payload.role: benign executable launched by the Run-key entry to confirm persistence execution through a marker file and debug string

persistence_behavior.value_name_transform: removes braces, hyphens, and spaces from MachineGuid

persistence_installer: RegSetValueExW used to write persistence value

registry: Run-key value name resembles normalized MachineGuid
process: A06_1a_registry_run_persistence.exe runs as the installer process
A06_1a_persistence_marker.exe executes after user logon or reboot
marker process records its PID and parent PID
marker process exits after writing confirmation artifact
file_system: marker file contains timestamp, PID, parent PID, process path, persistence type, trigger, and confirmation status
host: Procmon may record RegSetValue activity against the HKCU Run key
Regshot may show added Run-key value
Sysmon may record registry value set activity if configured
Sysmon or Procmon may record marker process creation during logon
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: MachineGuid retrieval, registry Run-key creation, and persistence value writing are implemented in the installer executable. Delayed execution, parent PID discovery, timestamp collection, marker file creation, and debug-string emission are implemented in the separate marker executable.
execution_trigger: The installer executes manually. The persistence payload executes automatically during subsequent user logon or reboot through the HKCU Run key.
execution_target: Current user's Run key and controlled marker executable at C:\Users\Public\A06_1a_persistence_marker.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates classic user-level Windows Run-key persistence where an autostart registry value causes a benign marker executable to run during user logon, producing host artifacts that confirm persistence installation and execution.

mitre_attack_mapping.note: Modern ATT&CK versions commonly represent this behavior under Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder.

control_notes.payload_effect: writes a controlled marker file confirming Run-key persistence execution

success_conditions: installer normalizes the MachineGuid by removing braces, hyphens, and spaces
installer writes a REG_SZ Run-key value
Run-key value name matches the normalized MachineGuid
user logs off and back on or reboots the Windows analysis VM
Windows launches A06_1a_persistence_marker.exe through the Run-key mechanism
marker waits briefly before writing its artifact
marker artifact records timestamp, PID, parent PID, process path, persistence type, execution trigger, and confirmation status
no network traffic or secondary payload download occurs
